title: MV/MZ Game Rescaling and Screen Resolution

posts.author: Oberoth-King
posts.body:
Greetings mates!
I'm in a bit of a pickle and could use some help. So, I'm working on a game using RPG Maker MZ, and I'm trying to set the resolution for the game scale without interfering with the illustrations that appear in conversations and cinematics, as well as the overall game resolution. Here's the snag: when I bump the resolution up to 1920x1080 (which matches the size of my illustrations for that sweet HD look), the game doesn't upscale the pixel art, everything ends up looking tiny, HUD and all. It just tweaks the games aspect ratio.
I've tried all sorts! Used a zoom plugin, but that messes with the illustrations too, i'd dropped the resolution to 640x480 and even tried a middle ground at 1280x720, but that just ruins the quality of my illustrations; they lose that crisp HD feel.
So, I'm on the hunt for a plugin or some workaround that lets me scale the pixel art without affecting the rest of the game. I want to run the game at 1920x1080, but have the pixel art appear as if it's at 640x720 in fullscreen. Hope that makes sense, 'cause this issue is so specific, I can't find a solution anywhere, and
it's driving me up the wall!

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
you can't and will never find a solution, because there is none.
"Resolution" is a term that has been very abused in the computer terminology.
Technically, a resolution is a number per distance - like dpi (dots per inch) for a printer.
As such the resolution is determined by your monitor, and physically fixed unless you change your monitor.
1280x720 is a screen size - and you can never mix screen sizes. That is because the pixel is the basic unit of every computer display.
you can switch between screen sizes, but that will cause a display reset and everything on the screen will always use the same screen size at the same time.
So theoretically you could switch to a different screen size for picture display, but that would still change the map as you see in your own examples.
There is absolutely no way around that, you can only usean image program to change the picture size to fewer pixels to fit the lower resolution - or use a grid resize plugin to use larger tiles (which has problems of its own as you can't change the editor)
